 WINK News Weather Authority meteorologists are tracking another windy day across Southwest Florida, with gusty winds, a few spotty showers and hazardous boating conditions continuing into midweek.
 Northeast winds will remain a big part of the forecast, with gusts reaching 35 mph during the afternoon. While most areas stay dry, a few passing showers are possible, mainly inland and across parts of Southwest Florida.
 Those winds are also steering in Atlantic moisture and more humidity, leading to a warmer start across SWFL in the lower 70s, about 3-5° above average. High temperatures will climb into the mid 80s today and above average in the upper 80s later this week into Halloween weekend. 
 Rain chances will gradually increase Wednesday and Thursday as more moisture moves in from the Atlantic. Spotty showers could become more widespread with rain coverage increasing to 30%. A few afternoon thunderstorms will also be possible through the weekend, with the best chances generally away from the immediate coast.
 Hazardous boating conditions continue
 Strong winds and rough seas will continue to create hazardous conditions across Southwest Florida's coastal waters into midweek. Wind gusts could approach gale force through this evening, making conditions especially dangerous for smaller boats.
 A moderate threat for rip currents is expected for local beaches today and tomorrow.
 Persistent offshore winds will also push water away from the coast, causing tides to run lower than normal through much of the week.
